title: Labneh balls
subtitle: Preserved strained yoghurt balls in herb oil
excerpt: Labneh balls are strained yoghurt rolled into small rounds and preserved in olive oil with herbs and spices. After a few days in the oil they become firmer, tangier, and deeply flavoured. They keep for weeks in the fridge and make an effortless centrepiece for a mezze spread or a gift for anyone who likes cheese.
sourceNotes: Labneh (strained yoghurt) is made across the Levant and is eaten as a dip, spread, or preserved in oil. The preserved ball form is particularly associated with Lebanon and Jordan and is a way of extending the life of labneh.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Must be made at least 4 days ahead to allow the labneh to firm and the oil to infuse. Keeps for 4 to 6 weeks in the fridge submerged in oil.

content.text: Labneh balls begin with yoghurt. Full-fat plain yoghurt is salted, hung in muslin for two days until much of the whey has drained away, leaving a dense, tangy mass. This labneh is then rolled into small balls and packed into a jar of olive oil with dried herbs, chilli, and spice.

After a few days in the oil, the balls firm further and take on the flavours of everything around them. After a week they are considerably more complex. They will keep in the fridge for up to six weeks as long as they stay covered in oil.
The leftover oil is flavoured and excellent. Use it to dress salads or dip bread.

items.prepNote: extra virgin, enough to submerge the balls

content.text: Mix the salt into the yoghurt. Line a large colander or sieve with a double layer of muslin cloth. Pour in the yoghurt mixture. Tie the ends of the muslin to make a bundle and hang over a bowl in the fridge, or rest the colander over a deep bowl. Leave for 2 days. The yoghurt will shrink considerably as whey drains away. The result should be a firm, dense labneh.
With clean, slightly damp hands, roll the labneh into balls about 3 cm across. Place on a clean plate as you go. Refrigerate uncovered for 2 hours to firm up slightly before jarring.

Mix the herbs and spices through the olive oil in a bowl. Place the labneh balls carefully into a sterilised jar and pour the herb oil over them until they are fully submerged. Seal the jar. Leave at room temperature for 24 hours, then refrigerate. The balls will be ready to eat after 4 days and at their best after a week.

rows.symptom: Labneh too soft to roll after 2 days
rows.cause: Yoghurt not hung long enough or muslin too loose
rows.fix: Return to the muslin and hang for another day. Full-fat yoghurt strains faster than low-fat.

rows.cause: Labneh too cold and stiff from fridge
rows.fix: Let the labneh sit at room temperature for 10 minutes before rolling; it becomes more pliable.

rows.cause: Olive oil does this at cold temperatures; it is normal
rows.fix: Remove the jar from the fridge 20 minutes before serving. The oil will return to liquid.

content.text: Roll the balls in zaatar spice blend, dried chilli flakes, or sesame seeds before placing in the oil for a coated version with more visual interest. Use goat's milk yoghurt for a sharper result.

Labneh balls are entirely a make-ahead recipe. They need at least 4 days and are better with a week. They keep for 4 to 6 weeks submerged in oil. Top up with more oil if the level drops to keep the balls covered.

Labneh is a daily part of breakfast across the Levant. The preserved ball form is associated with the Lebanese and Jordanian countryside, where yoghurt is made in quantity and labneh balls are a practical way to extend it through the year. They appear on mezze tables, at breakfast with bread and olives, and are sold in jars at Lebanese food shops.
